prompt:
Find real, published benchmarks comparing SQLite and DuckDB query performance on analytical workloads. Cite the sources and the specific numbers they report.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are the real, published benchmarks I found comparing SQLite and DuckDB query performance on analytical workloads, formatted as required.

SOURCE: https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/data-science/a_database_for_analysis_rows_columns_indexes/ | QUOTE: "On the four analytical queries the column store wins by a factor of 11 to 97 with a single thread, and by 120 to 270 with all of them." | CLAIM: DuckDB outperforms SQLite on analytical queries by 11x to 97x when using a single thread, and by 120x to 270x when using all available threads.
SOURCE: https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/data-science/a_database_for_analysis_rows_columns_indexes/ | QUOTE: "Fetching 2,000 complete orders by key takes SQLite 34 milliseconds, 17 microseconds each. DuckDB takes more than a second, 570 microseconds each, although it too has an index on the key, and adding threads makes it slower." | CLAIM: SQLite is significantly faster than DuckDB for point lookups, taking 34ms for 2,000 key fetches versus DuckDB's over one second.
SOURCE: https://zaynetro.com/post/2023-playing-with-olap | QUOTE: "| Count by event_type | 700ms | 10ms | 25ms | 80ms |" | CLAIM: For a "Count by event_type" query, SQLite took 700ms while DuckDB took 10ms, indicating a 70x speed advantage for DuckDB.
SOURCE: https://zaynetro.com/post/2023-playing-with-olap | QUOTE: "| Average feedback score | 255ms | 35ms | 160ms | — |" | CLAIM: For an "Average feedback score" query, SQLite took 255ms while DuckDB took 35ms, showing DuckDB performing roughly 7x faster.
SOURCE: https://zaynetro.com/post/2023-playing-with-olap | QUOTE: "| Count by event_type | 10350ms | 70ms | 200ms | 775ms |" | CLAIM: On a larger dataset for "Count by event_type", SQLite took 10,350ms compared to DuckDB's 70ms, a performance difference of approximately 148x.
SOURCE: https://zaynetro.com/post/2023-playing-with-olap | QUOTE: "| Form submissions by page | 12340ms | 620ms (650ms) | 6980ms | 9380ms |" | CLAIM: For a "Form submissions by page" query on a larger dataset, SQLite took 12,340ms while DuckDB took 620ms, demonstrating nearly 20x better performance by DuckDB.
SOURCE: https://github.com/marvelousmlops/database_comparison/blob/master/README.md | QUOTE: "| Aggregation query              | 0.00427 seconds        | 0.26850 seconds        | 722.87220 seconds       | 0.00348 seconds     | 0.27129 seconds     |" | CLAIM: For aggregation queries, DuckDB without an index took 0.00427 seconds while SQLite without an index took 0.26850 seconds, making DuckDB roughly 63x faster.
SOURCE: https://github.com/marvelousmlops/database_comparison/blob/master/README.md | QUOTE: "| Query by ID                    | 0.00281 seconds        | 0.03814 seconds        | 0.00188 seconds         | 0.00121 seconds     | 0.00056 seconds     |" | CLAIM: For point lookups by ID without an index, DuckDB (0.00281s) is faster than SQLite (0.03814s), but with an index, SQLite (0.00056s) outperforms DuckDB (0.00121s).
SOURCE: https://junaidhasan.com/assets/report-cse544.pdf | QUOTE: "DuckDB executed this query in 0.22 seconds, whereas SQLite took 349 sec onds (a 1,500x difference)." | CLAIM: DuckDB executed an analytical query in 0.22 seconds while SQLite took 349 seconds, representing a 1,500x performance difference.
SOURCE: https://marending.dev/notes/sqlite-vs-duckdb/ | QUOTE: "Clearly, DuckDB is faster across the board." | CLAIM: DuckDB is faster than SQLite across analytical workloads.
SOURCE: https://marending.dev/notes/sqlite-vs-duckdb/ | QUOTE: "DuckDB is storing the data significantly more compactly, too. 20 MB for the database file versus 60-80 MB with SQLite depending on indices." | CLAIM: DuckDB stores analytical data more compactly, using 20MB compared to SQLite's 60-80MB for the same dataset.
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: specific benchmark comparing SQLite and DuckDB on TPC-H or TPC-DS analytical workloads
